### Expected Behavior

It should result in an error, similar to https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/pull/38628

### Actual Behavior

It will cause panic.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terraform init`

### Additional Context

`value.AsString() will cause a panic for marked values.

This is the same issue as https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/38694. `value.AsString()` causes a panic for null values.
https://github.com/zclconf/go-cty/blob/v1.18.0/cty/value_ops.go#L1460-L1462

The https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/pull/38628 fix does not account for the case where the value after evaluation is null.

Just to be clear, this issue did not occur in actual production code. It was discovered during white-box testing when [supporting dynamic module sources in TFLint](https://github.com/terraform-linters/tflint/pull/2521), and such cases are likely to be rare in practice.

### References

- https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/pull/38217

title: HTTP backend: TLS config defaults to TLS 1.0, allows protocol downgrade
need_summary: Whether the HTTP backend really permits a TLS downgrade is answered by Go's crypto/tls documentation showing Config.MinVersion defaults to TLS 1.2, not TLS 1.0.
security_topic: TLS minimum version default and downgrade risk
question_text: The HTTP backend should enforce TLS 1.2 as the minimum protocol version, consistent with the OCI backend (`internal/backend/remote-state/oci/auth.go:323`) and the deprecation of TLS 1.0/1.1 per [RFC 8996](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8996) (March 2021).
answer_text: The http backend currently uses TLS 1.2.  When calling code doesn't set Config.MinVersion it [defaults to TLS 1.2 by default](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/tls#Config.MinVersion):
thread_text:
ISSUE #38576: HTTP backend: TLS config defaults to TLS 1.0, allows protocol downgrade
Author: SebTardif
Date: 2026-05-13T21:48:43Z
Labels: bug, new
State: closed

[c0]
### Terraform Version

```
Terraform v1.16.0-dev (main branch, HEAD)
```

### Terraform Configuration Files

This is an internal code issue in the HTTP backend TLS configuration, not triggered by a specific user config. Any configuration using the HTTP backend with TLS client certificates is affected:

```terraform
terraform {
  backend "http" {
    address        = "https://example.com/state"
    client_cert_file = "/path/to/cert.pem"
    client_key_file  = "/path/to/key.pem"
  }
}
```

### Debug Output

No debug output needed. The issue is visible in the source code at `internal/backend/remote-state/http/backend.go` in the `configureTLS` function: the `tls.Config` is created without setting `MinVersion`, which defaults to TLS 1.0.

### Expected Behavior

The HTTP backend should enforce TLS 1.2 as the minimum protocol version, consistent with the OCI backend (`internal/backend/remote-state/oci/auth.go:323`) and the deprecation of TLS 1.0/1.1 per [RFC 8996](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8996) (March 2021).

### Actual Behavior

The `tls.Config` created by `configureTLS` uses Go's default `MinVersion` of 0, which permits TLS 1.0 and 1.1 connections. This allows protocol downgrade attacks against state data in transit.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Review `internal/backend/remote-state/http/backend.go`, function `configureTLS`
2. Note that `tls.Config{}` is created without `MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12`
3. Compare with OCI backend at `internal/backend/remote-state/oci/auth.go:323` which correctly sets `MinVersion`

### Additional Context

The omission was introduced in #34806 (2024-03-05) during the `helper/schema` refactoring. I intend to submit a fix for this issue and have a working implementation on my fork.

### References

- #34806 (introduced the omission)
- [moby/moby#32056](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/32056) (Docker/Moby added TLS minimum version enforcement for the same class of downgrade risk)
- Previously submitted as #38546 (closed; resubmitting with issue-first workflow per Contributing.md)
- Fork branch with fix: [`SebTardif/terraform@fix/http-backend-tls-minversion`](https://github.com/SebTardif/terraform/tree/fix/http-backend-tls-minversion)

title: GPG error when trying to download 1.14.8
need_summary: Whether the expired PGP key verification failure was a real security-relevant release-signature issue and what fixed it, anchored by the maintainer’s note that hc-install v0.9.4 addressed the verification errors and the Terraform 1.14.9 release update.
security_topic: PGP signature verification failure due to expired signing key
question_text: Any idea when this will be resolved? Will fixes be backported to all the older versions? We are seeing failures in 1.11.4.
answer_text:
@yermulnik Right now there is no secondary location for the old key. Sorry. We checked Keybase, but it only supports a single key.

---

I'm going to close this issue for now. A couple of things were addressed by different teams:

* The team released a new version of hc-install ([0.9.4](https://github.com/hashicorp/hc-install/releases/tag/v0.9.4)) that addresses the verification errors. It may take some time for all the downstream tools to update their dependencies and release new versions. You will then need to upgrade your local version (e.g. `tfswitch` or Atlantis).
* https://www.hashicorp.com/.well-known/pgp-key.txt now only contains a single key. It's the new, valid key. Other tools should therefore be working again if they just check the first key.
* For Terraform Stacks users, we have released an updated Terraform version (see [1.14.9](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/releases/tag/v1.14.9) and [1.15.0-rc3](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/releases/tag/v1.15.0-rc3)).

Sorry for the disruption. There isn't anything else we can do in Terraform, so I will close the issue. If you are still experiencing issues, please check if your tool of choice has been updated. If not, raise an issue in their tracker. Alternatively, feel free to create a new issue here if you think it is Terraform-related.

thread_text:
ISSUE #38273: PGP key refresh broke signature verification for tools using go-crypto/openpgp/v2
Author: DionJones615
Date: 2026-03-12T21:39:04Z
Labels: question
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

HashiCorp's recent PGP key refresh (around 2026-02-18) extended subkey expiry dates from 2026 to 2030 on key `C874011F0AB405110D02105534365D9472D7468F`. However, the updated key export at `https://www.hashicorp.com/.well-known/pgp-key.txt` only contains the **new** UID self-certification (dated 2026-02-18) — the previous self-certification was not preserved.

This breaks any tool that uses ProtonMail's `go-crypto/openpgp/v2` (or `gopenpgp/v3`) to verify Terraform release signatures. These libraries perform temporal validation: they require a UID self-certification that **predates** the signature being verified. Since the only self-certification is now from 2026-02-18, any release signed before that date fails with:

```
no valid self signature found
```

## Impact

| Terraform version | Signed | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| 1.9.8 | 2024-10-16 | ❌ FAIL |
| 1.11.2 | 2025-03-12 | ❌ FAIL |
| 1.14.5 | 2026-02-11 | ❌ FAIL |
| 1.14.7 | 2026-03-11 | ✅ PASS |

This is actively impacting users of `terraform-switcher` ([warrensbox/terraform-switcher#722](https://github.com/warrensbox/terraform-switcher/issues/722)) and likely any other Go-based tooling that verifies Terraform release signatures using `go-crypto` v2.

Standard `gpg --verify` is unaffected — this only impacts programmatic verification via the stricter go-crypto library.

## Suggested Fix

Re-export the PGP key preserving the old self-certification alongside the new one. If both are still on the signing keyring, `gpg --export C874011F0AB405110D02105534365D9472D7468F` should produce an export containing both self-certifications. This is standard PGP practice — key servers accumulate all self-signatures for exactly this reason.

## Key comparison

Old key (working):
```
pub  4096R/72D7468F 2021-04-19
sub  4096R/2379BA9A 2021-04-19 [expires: 2026-04-18]
sub  4096R/7685B676 2021-04-19 [expires: 2022-04-20]
sub  4096R/CD27AB87 2021-04-21 [expires: 2026-04-20]
```

New key (breaks pre-2026-02-18 signatures):
```
pub  4096R/72D7468F 2021-04-19
sub  4096R/2379BA9A 2021-04-19 [expires: 2030-03-01]
sub  4096R/7685B676 2021-04-19 [expires: 2022-04-20]
sub  4096R/CD27AB87 2021-04-21 [expires: 2030-03-01]
```

The subkey expiry extensions are fine — the issue is solely that the old UID self-certification was dropped from the export.

title: Provider-signing certificate seems to have expired
need_summary: Whether the expired HashiCorp code-signing certificate affects loading the random provider on Windows, with the workaround of pinning hashicorp/random to 3.7.2 because Windows verifies the signature based on signing date.
security_topic: provider code-signing certificate expiration affecting Windows execution
question_text:
### Expected Behavior

I would have expected a random pet resource to be created
answer_text:
We are aware of the expired certificate and are working on renewing it. As far as I know, this should only affect the random provider, and other providers should work as usual. 

In the meantime, if you pin the random provider to version 3.7.2, everything should work, as Windows verifies the signature based on the signing date.

title: S3 Backend: AWS_USE_FIPS_ENDPOINT incorrectly enables FIPS endpoints — env variable is not parsed as boolean
need_summary: Whether AWS_USE_FIPS_ENDPOINT false-like values should disable FIPS endpoints, and the answer is anchored by the maintainer’s reference to issue #33765, fix #37940, and the AWS SDK for Go env parsing behavior.
security_topic: environment-variable boolean parsing leading to unintended FIPS endpoint enablement
question_text:
Environment variable `AWS_USE_FIPS_ENDPOINT` =  "false" or false (case-insensitive) should result in FIPS endpoints NOT being enabled.
Only setting "true", true, should enable FIPS.
answer_text:
Hello and thank you for the bug report. This was introduced via #33765 in `v1.6.0`. 

Parsing of the variable should match the AWS SDK for Go (see [here](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/blob/3daa74a863790060e074bbf3455e02f8bf478c48/config/env_config.go#L836-L845) and [here](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/blob/3daa74a863790060e074bbf3455e02f8bf478c48/config/env_config.go#L857-L866)), but we incorrectly treated any non-empty value as `true` instead. It's possible this was to match some behavior in the AWS provider or `aws-sdk-go-base` library at the time, but from what I can tell nothing like this still exists for these configuration options today. 

With this context, I believe we should apply the fix from #37940, which ignores any value that is not `true` or `false`. This matches the behavior of the AWS SDK for Go (and therefore the AWS and AWSCC providers). Technically this represents a breaking change, even if to correct a long standing bug. Because the S3 backend is tied to the Terraform CLI release cycle we are unable to increment the major version and will instead plan to apply the fix in the next minor release (`v1.15.0`), consistent with how breaking backend changes have been made previously.

title: Security: address authentication bypass flags and credential handling in backend configurations
need_summary: Whether Terraform’s backend security settings like skip_cert_verification and S3 skip_* flags are intentional and how they should be documented, with the answer anchored in the maintainer’s security policy page and the referenced docs PRs #983 and #984.
security_topic: applicability of intentional backend bypass flags and secure configuration guidance
question_text:
Hi HashiCorp Terraform team,

Thank you for maintaining the cornerstone of infrastructure-as-code — Terraform's impact on secure infrastructure management is immeasurable.

While reviewing backend security configurations, we identified several settings that could compromise security in production environments:

## 1) Authentication bypass flags in S3 backend (P1)
**Location**: `/internal/backend/remote-state/s3/backend.go` lines 193-207
```go
"skip_credentials_validation": {
    Description: "Skip the credentials validation via STS API..."
},
"skip_requesting_account_id": {...},
"skip_metadata_api_check": {...}
```
**Risk**: These flags allow bypassing critical AWS security validations, potentially enabling unauthorized access to resources and circumventing IAM controls.

## 2) TLS certificate verification bypass (P1) 
**Location**: `/internal/backend/remote-state/http/backend.go` lines 73-77
```go
"skip_cert_verification": {
    Description: "Whether to skip TLS verification"
}
```
**Risk**: Enables man-in-the-middle attacks on state file transfers, compromising state integrity.

## 3) Hardcoded credentials in test examples (P2)
**Locations**: Multiple test files including:
- `/internal/terraform/testdata/input-provider-with-vars-and-module/main.tf:2`
- `/internal/command/testdata/validate-invalid/multiple_providers/main.tf:2-3,8-9`

```terraform
provider "aws" {
  access_key = "abc123"
  secret_key = "b" 
}
```

**Risk**: These examples may be copied by users, leading to credential exposure in production configurations.

## 4) Missing sensitive field marking (P2)
**Location**: `/internal/backend/remote-state/s3/backend.go` lines 141-145
```go
"secret_key": {
    // Missing: Sensitive: true,
}
```
**Risk**: AWS secret keys could be exposed in logs or console output.

## Proposed remediation:
- Add security warnings for authentication bypass flags with explicit acknowledgment requirements
- Deprecate or remove `skip_cert_verification` with migration guidance  
- Replace hardcoded test credentials with placeholder values and security guidance
- Mark all credential fields as `Sensitive: true`
- Add documentation emphasizing secure backend configuration patterns

These changes would strengthen Terraform's security posture while maintaining backward compatibility through deprecation cycles.

Context: This analysis is from FlowSpec Configuration Security Review Team.

Thanks for considering these security improvements to protect the infrastructure-as-code ecosystem.
answer_text:
Hi @youming1970,

These are intentional decisions within the software, which are not enabled by default. Please see the security policy page here: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/security/policy. If you have security concerns, you can reach out to [security@hashicorp.com](mailto:security@hashicorp.com).

Thanks!

comments.body:
Hi HashiCorp Terraform team,

Thank you for maintaining the cornerstone of infrastructure-as-code — Terraform's impact on secure infrastructure management is immeasurable.

While reviewing backend security configurations, we identified several settings that could compromise security in production environments:

## 1) Authentication bypass flags in S3 backend (P1)
**Location**: `/internal/backend/remote-state/s3/backend.go` lines 193-207
```go
"skip_credentials_validation": {
    Description: "Skip the credentials validation via STS API..."
},
"skip_requesting_account_id": {...},
"skip_metadata_api_check": {...}
```
**Risk**: These flags allow bypassing critical AWS security validations, potentially enabling unauthorized access to resources and circumventing IAM controls.

## 2) TLS certificate verification bypass (P1) 
**Location**: `/internal/backend/remote-state/http/backend.go` lines 73-77
```go
"skip_cert_verification": {
    Description: "Whether to skip TLS verification"
}
```
**Risk**: Enables man-in-the-middle attacks on state file transfers, compromising state integrity.

## 3) Hardcoded credentials in test examples (P2)
**Locations**: Multiple test files including:
- `/internal/terraform/testdata/input-provider-with-vars-and-module/main.tf:2`
- `/internal/command/testdata/validate-invalid/multiple_providers/main.tf:2-3,8-9`

```terraform
provider "aws" {
  access_key = "abc123"
  secret_key = "b" 
}
```
**Risk**: These examples may be copied by users, leading to credential exposure in production configurations.

## 4) Missing sensitive field marking (P2)
**Location**: `/internal/backend/remote-state/s3/backend.go` lines 141-145
```go
"secret_key": {
    // Missing: Sensitive: true,
}
```
**Risk**: AWS secret keys could be exposed in logs or console output.

## Proposed remediation:
- Add security warnings for authentication bypass flags with explicit acknowledgment requirements
- Deprecate or remove `skip_cert_verification` with migration guidance  
- Replace hardcoded test credentials with placeholder values and security guidance
- Mark all credential fields as `Sensitive: true`
- Add documentation emphasizing secure backend configuration patterns

These changes would strengthen Terraform's security posture while maintaining backward compatibility through deprecation cycles.

Context: This analysis is from FlowSpec Configuration Security Review Team.

Thanks for considering these security improvements to protect the infrastructure-as-code ecosystem.

title: Terraform plans fail due to "inconsistent final plan" for referenced values that change, despite using the legacy plugin SDK
need_summary: Whether Terraform’s documented legacy-plugin-sdk consistency behavior intentionally causes downstream resources to error when they reference an attribute whose value changes, as described in the Terraform plugin SDKv2 data-consistency-errors docs.
security_topic: legacy provider plan inconsistency propagation across referenced values
question_text:
If `google_logging_log_view_iam_policy` references the `bucket` field on a `google_logging_log_view`, and it changes during apply (which is allowed by the legacy plugin SDK), the IAM policy resource will fail to apply with an "inconsistent plan" error.

I would expect this tolerance to extend to resources that _reference_ the changed field.
answer_text:
Hi @melinath,

Yes, what you're seeing is the _result_ of allowing the behavior that the logs are warning about. We allow certain inconsistencies in the plan for legacy providers, but the extent of what is allowed was essentially frozen many years ago. The changes are usually just a minor annoyance when they in isolation, preventing resource from cleanly applying. When those invalid changes are propagated between resources however, they cause errors we cannot handle because another resource's plan has become invalid, and that resource might not be equipped to handle the bad data -- it might not even be from the same provider. This is what `confusing errors from downstream operations` is referring to.

This appears to be described on https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/data-consistency-errors:

> If a problematic attribute value is referenced by another resource in the same Terraform configuration, Terraform will raise an error diagnostic for the downstream resource due to the unexpected value behavior caused by the upstream resource. This often will cause a confusing bug report in the downstream provider, which cannot be fixed there.

If this is talking about the same thing - I would argue that Terraform's behavior should change, so that it's not causing confusing errors for resources that haven't yet migrated to the plugin-framework.

comments.author: jbardin
comments.body:
Hi @melinath,

Yes, what you're seeing is the _result_ of allowing the behavior that the logs are warning about. We allow certain inconsistencies in the plan for legacy providers, but the extent of what is allowed was essentially frozen many years ago. The changes are usually just a minor annoyance when they in isolation, preventing resource from cleanly applying. When those invalid changes are propagated between resources however, they cause errors we cannot handle because another resource's plan has become invalid, and that resource might not be equipped to handle the bad data -- it might not even be from the same provider. This is what `confusing errors from downstream operations` is referring to.

thread_text:
ISSUE #37151: Security: Vulnerabilities in K8s apimachinery and Consul API dependencies
Author: Ilhan-Personal
Date: 2025-05-22T07:12:28Z
Labels: enhancement, new
State: closed

[c0]
### Terraform Version

```shell
latest
```

### Use Cases

Two security vulnerabilities have been identified in our dependencies:
K8s apimachinery package vulnerability
Package: k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime v0.25.5
Severity: High
Type: Denial of Service (DoS)
Reference: https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-GOLANG-K8SIOAPIMACHINERYPKGUTILRUNTIME-8367153
Fixed version: v0.29.0-alpha.3 and later
HashiCorp Consul API potential security concerns
Package: HashiCorp Consul API
Fixed version: v1.32.1
Note: This issue was previously raised to the security team but no reply was received. Therefore, I'm creating this public issue and corresponding PR to address these vulnerabilities.


### Attempted Solutions

I've attempted to resolve these vulnerabilities by investigating the current dependencies in use. In the process, I confirmed that Terraform is using outdated versions of the affected packages:
k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime v0.25.5 which contains the high severity DoS vulnerability
An outdated HashiCorp Consul API version with potential security concerns
I've verified through testing that simply updating these dependencies resolves the issues without breaking functionality. Build tests confirm that Terraform builds successfully with the updated dependencies.


### Proposal

I propose updating the following dependencies to their secure versions:
For Kubernetes-related packages:
Update k8s.io/api to v0.33.0
Update k8s.io/apimachinery to v0.33.0
Update k8s.io/client-go to v0.33.0
Update k8s.io/utils to v0.33.0
For HashiCorp Consul API:
Update to v1.32.1
These updates should be applied to both the main module and the Kubernetes remote state backend module. This approach addresses the security vulnerabilities while maintaining compatibility with the existing codebase.

title: Terraform Crash During Redeploy After Initial Deployment
need_summary: Whether the Terraform crash on redeploy is the same as duplicate issue #36184, with the maintainer explicitly pointing to that issue and a fileset-based for_each/external-files-changing-during-apply explanation.
security_topic: terraform crash during redeploy due to file-derived for_each expansion
question_text:
Hello Terraform Support Team,

I am encountering a critical issue where Terraform crashes when attempting to redeploy my infrastructure after performing a destroy operation. The initial deployment proceeds without any issues, but subsequent destroy and redeploy actions result in a crash with a panic error.

Steps to Reproduce:

Initial Deployment:
Run terraform init to initialize the Terraform configuration.
Execute terraform apply to deploy the infrastructure.
The deployment completes successfully.
Destroy Infrastructure:
Run terraform destroy to remove the deployed infrastructure.
The destroy operation completes without errors.
Redeploy Infrastructure:
Execute terraform apply again to redeploy the infrastructure.
Terraform crashes during this step with the error detailed below.
Expected Behavior:

After destroying the infrastructure, running terraform apply should redeploy the resources successfully, just like the initial deployment.
answer_text: Given that the module expansion is using what looks like a file name for the key, I'm guessing you might be using `fileset` to generate the input to that `for_each` expression, and this is a duplicate of #36184. Is it possible that you are depending on external files which are changing during apply?

### Expected Behavior

Hello Terraform Support Team,

I am encountering a critical issue where Terraform crashes when attempting to redeploy my infrastructure after performing a destroy operation. The initial deployment proceeds without any issues, but subsequent destroy and redeploy actions result in a crash with a panic error.

Steps to Reproduce:

Initial Deployment:
Run terraform init to initialize the Terraform configuration.
Execute terraform apply to deploy the infrastructure.
The deployment completes successfully.
Destroy Infrastructure:
Run terraform destroy to remove the deployed infrastructure.
The destroy operation completes without errors.
Redeploy Infrastructure:
Execute terraform apply again to redeploy the infrastructure.
Terraform crashes during this step with the error detailed below.
Expected Behavior:

After destroying the infrastructure, running terraform apply should redeploy the resources successfully, just like the initial deployment.

Hello Terraform Support Team,

I am encountering a critical issue where Terraform crashes when attempting to redeploy my infrastructure after performing a destroy operation. The initial deployment proceeds without any issues, but subsequent destroy and redeploy actions result in a crash with a panic error.

Execute terraform apply to deploy the infrastructure.
The deployment completes successfully.
Destroy Infrastructure:

Redeploy Infrastructure:

comments.body:
Hi @Maher2123,

The error indicates there was a problem getting the value for `var.team_config_data`, but the portion of the configuration you've shared does not include any references to that variable. We are also missing the call to the `rules_process_team_configuration` module showing how that is expanded. I don't know what `terraform deploy` is meant to be, was that meant to be another `terraform apply`?

Given that the module expansion is using what looks like a file name for the key, I'm guessing you might be using `fileset` to generate the input to that `for_each` expression, and this is a duplicate of #36184. Is it possible that you are depending on external files which are changing during apply?

title: Inconsistent TF_TOKEN use in provider HTTP calls
need_summary: Whether Terraform’s provider installation follow-up requests intentionally omit credentials, with the answer anchored in the provider network mirror protocol docs and the Terraform v1.11 .netrc support note plus issue #29349.
security_topic: credentials not sent on provider archive download requests
question_text: The TF_TOKEN should be used for all HTTP calls made to install the provider.
answer_text:
Hi @fancybear-dev, Terraform is behaving as documented in this instance: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/provider-network-mirror-protocol#authentication

Specifically:

> Terraform does not send credentials when retrieving the archives whose URLs are given in the "List Available Installation Packages" response below. If a particular mirror considers the distribution packages themselves to be sensitive then it must use cryptographically-secure, user-specific, and time-limited URLs in the metadata response. Strategies for doing so are out of scope of this protocol documentation.

The next version of Terraform (v1.11) will support using a `.netrc` file to support adding credentials to the follow up requests, which may work for you in the short term: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/v1.11.x/providers#private-providers

In the longer term, please follow this enhancement requests for updates on this issue more generally: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/29349

Thanks!

title: Fix vulnerability reported by Prisma Cloud on module github.com/emicklei/go-restful/v3
need_summary: Whether the Prisma Cloud-reported vulnerability in the indirect dependency github.com/emicklei/go-restful/v3 is relevant, with the answer anchored by the cited fix version v3.10.0+ and the linked huntr advisory page.
security_topic: applicability of scanner-reported dependency vulnerability
question_text:
Terraform Version

```shell
Terraform v1.10.4
on darwin_arm64
```

### Use Cases

[Prisma Cloud](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/prisma/cloud) container vulnerability scanning reports a vulnerability on the indirect dependency github.com/emicklei/go-restful/v3 used in `internal/backend/remote-state/kubernetes`
For reference: within the Prisma Cloud ecosystem, this vulnerability is referred to as PRISMA-2022-0227, rated 7.5 - High. The vulnerability is fixed in versions v.3.10.0 and upwards of github.com/emicklei/go-restful/v3.
A similar question was asked on HashiCorp Discuss [here](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/security-vulnerability-prisma-2022-0227/51264). To illustrate, a similar issue was raised on Kubernetes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120604.
answer_text: Vulnerability scanners tend to flag false positives in terms of code paths with vulnerabilities that are not used by the actual product. In these cases, the dependency in question will be updated the next time there is a functional need to do so. In the case of backends not maintained by the core team, as in this case, it may take some time as the backends tend not to be the highest priority for those teams.

title: Proposal: store sensitive values in state as a hash rather than the value itself
need_summary: Whether Terraform can avoid storing secrets in state by hashing them instead, and the answer cites the provider plugin protocol plus HashiCorp’s Ephemeral Values blog post as the concrete source.
security_topic: storing sensitive values in Terraform state
question_text:
### Proposal

Terraform obviously stores all values (including sensitive values) in state which is not secure.

My suggestion is to store a hash of sensitive values in state rather than the value itself, that way sensitive values could be stored in state and terraform would still know if it needs to replace resources without violating security principals or requiring a seperate solution to manage secrets independently of the stack.

Thoughts?
answer_text:
Hi @jamesla,

The provider plugin protocol requires the values saved by the provider are always returned to the provider unchanged, they cannot be changed in the state. The new [Ephemeral Values](https://www.hashicorp.com/blog/terraform-1-10-improves-handling-secrets-in-state-with-ephemeral-values) project is working towards a new system for avoiding stored secrets in the state.

question_text:

### Actual Behavior

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @bschaatsbergen 2024-11-27T14:01:59Z:
Hey @BroMattMiller,

Thank you for reporting this! The S3 backend is managed by the AWS Provider team at HashiCorp, and this issue has been added to their triage queue. Thanks again!
---
[c2] @bschaatsbergen 2024-11-27T14:03:04Z:
Based on your debug logs, I noticed references to object locking. Could you confirm if S3 Object Lock is enabled on your bucket, and if default retention is enabled, as this is often used to prevent deletion and overwriting of files? AFAIK, the `Content-MD5` or `x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm` header is required for any request to upload an object with a retention period configured using Object Lock.

Please note that the lock file is expected to be written to the S3 bucket and deleted when the lock is cleaned up, which could potentially conflict with how Object Lock is configured on the S3 bucket.

I haven’t been able to replicate this issue with an S3 bucket that has Object Lock enabled but default retention disabled. I’ll take some time to set up an S3 bucket with both Object Lock and default retention enabled to investigate further and get back to you as soon as I have an update.

**Update**: I can replicate the issue with an S3 bucket configured with Object Lock and default retention set to Governance for X days.
---
[c3] @BroMattMiller 2024-11-27T14:24:30Z:
Yes, I have enabled Object Lock, per AWS Security Hub control S3.15, "S3 general purpose buckets should have Object Lock enabled." The retention mode is Governance and the retention date is 30 days. The credentials used by Terraform do have the necessary privileges to override this.
---
[c4] @bschaatsbergen 2024-11-27T16:20:42Z:
For some additional context, when S3 Object Lock is enabled on a bucket with a retention period, Amazon S3 requires the `Content-MD5` or` x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm` header for object uploads via PutObject to ensure data integrity during the upload process. For more details, see [Uploading objects to an Object Lock enabled bucket](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-managing.html#object-lock-managing-events).

It appears that the default behavior of the `skip_checksum` flag for the lock file was not maintained when writing the lock file to S3 Object Lock-enabled buckets.

To clarify the default behavior of `skip_checksum`: by default, if this argument is not set in the backend, we set the S3 checksum algorithm behavior to SHA256. This causes the underlying S3 AWS SDK V2 serializers to automatically append the that required `x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm` header. For more details, see the relevant code in the [AWS SDK v2 serializers](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/blob/8939ed049c8b3490f9a3dbd4e4d3d56cf22a27f2/service/s3/serializers.go#L7494-L7497).

I think it should be possible to swap out the current base S3 client with the [s3manager](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/tree/8939ed049c8b3490f9a3dbd4e4d3d56cf22a27f2/feature/s3/manager) to handle writing lock files to S3 Object Lock-enabled buckets the same way as we write state, and perserve the default behavior of `skip_checksum` when writing a lock file too.
---

Hey @BroMattMiller,

This should now be fixed in Terraform 1.10.1—thank you again for taking the time to bring this to our attention.

ISSUE #36067: CVE's found in Terraform (outdated libraries)
Author: sbstn-dev
Date: 2024-11-20T20:35:46Z
Labels: bug, new
State: closed

[c0]
### Terraform Version

```shell
1.9.8
```


### Terraform Configuration Files

-

### Debug Output

-

### Expected Behavior

AWS Security Inspector (or other tool) don't reported CVE vulnerabilities

### Actual Behavior

AWS Security Inspector findings CVE vulnerabilities in additional libraries 

### Steps to Reproduce

1. add terraform package to Dockerfile
2. build image
3. push image to AWS ECR

### Additional Context

CVE-2024-10006 - github.com/hashicorp/consul/api
CVE-2024-10005 - github.com/hashicorp/consul/api
	
A vulnerability was identified in Consul and Consul Enterprise (“Consul”) such that using Headers in L7 traffic intentions could bypass HTTP header based access rules.

Installed version: v1.13.0 

Fixed version: 1.20.1

CVE-2024-51744 - github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4

golang-jwt is a Go implementation of JSON Web Tokens. Unclear documentation of the error behavior in `ParseWithClaims` can lead to situation where users are potentially not checking errors in the way they should be. Especially, if a token is both expired and invalid, the errors returned by `ParseWithClaims` return both error codes. If users only check for the `jwt.ErrTokenExpired ` using `error.Is`, they will ignore the embedded `jwt.ErrTokenSignatureInvalid` and thus potentially accept invalid tokens. A fix has been back-ported with the error handling logic from the `v5` branch to the `v4` branch. In this logic, the `ParseWithClaims` function will immediately return in "dangerous" situations (e.g., an invalid signature), limiting the combined errors only to situations where the signature is valid, but further validation failed (e.g., if the signature is valid, but is expired AND has the wrong audience). This fix is part of the 4.5.1 release. We are aware that this changes the behaviour of an established func

Installed version: v4.4.2

Fixed version: v4.5.1

### References

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

The download URL `https://ar-terraform-registry.us-central1.run.app/download/provider/tf-registry-backend/asset/random:3.6.3-darwin-arm64:terraform-provider-random_3.6.3_SHA256SUMS` is also behind the same host. Since I've configured `~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json`, I expected Terraform to use the credential I added there for the downloads.

### Actual Behavior

As shown in the debug output, Terraform failed to download the file because it's not using the credential I have specified. I also confirmed that the server side didn't receive any bearer token. It seems Terraform _assumes_ the download URLs are publicly accessible.

Also notice, the previous calls for service discovery and getting version (e.g. `GET https://ar-terraform-registry.us-central1.run.app/v1/providers/tf-registry-backend/random/3.6.3/download/darwin/arm64`) were all successful because Terraform used the auth token in those requests. It's only the **download** call that's impacted.

### Steps to Reproduce

I can't make the service accessible to you. But I'd expect any other custom private registry will have the same problem if the download URLs require authentication.

### Additional Context

I also tried to set `TF_TOKEN_ar__terraform__registry_us__central1_run_app` to my auth token per https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/config/config-file#environment-variable-credentials. The result is the same. The download requests didn't honor this config.

The other reference is https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/provider-registry-protocol#response-properties-1. It doesn't have _any_ mentioning that the download URLs **must** be public accessible links.

[c1] @liamcervante 2024-11-15T16:10:09Z:
Hi @yolocs, thanks for filing this.

I can confirm that Terraform isn't attaching authentication to the follow up requests when retrieving the `downloadUrl` and the `shasumUrl`. This is because both the public and private registries return publicly available URLs for these attributes. This means that it is difficult for us to change this without breaking our primary points of integration.

I do agree that this behaviour isn't documented, I've tagged this issue as a documentation improvement and raised with the internal docs team.

Could you attach temporary credentials to the returned URLs? Or copy the behaviour of the private registry which returns temporary unauthenticated endpoints?

Thanks!
---
[c2] @yolocs 2024-11-15T17:48:15Z:
Thanks for the prompt response!

A somewhat low risk change could be expanding the CLI config to indicate that downloads should also attach auth token. E.g.

```
{
  "credentials": {
    "ar-terraform-registry.us-central1.run.app": {
      "token": "eyJh...",
      "attachToDownloads": true
    }
  }
}
```

Existing user journeys should not be interrupted since it's a new config field.

> Could you attach temporary credentials to the returned URLs? Or copy the behaviour of the private registry which returns temporary unauthenticated endpoints?

While it's possible, it's definitely not trivial. Not every storage system comes with a signed URL feature, in which case registry implementors would have to build their own signed URLs and signing keys, etc. Plus, having publicly accessible URLs, though temporary, increases the risk of data exfiltration. And that partly forfeits the purpose of having a _private_ registry.
---

The download URL `https://ar-terraform-registry.us-central1.run.app/download/provider/tf-registry-backend/asset/random:3.6.3-darwin-arm64:terraform-provider-random_3.6.3_SHA256SUMS` is also behind the same host. Since I've configured `~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json`, I expected Terraform to use the credential I added there for the downloads.

### Actual Behavior

As shown in the debug output, Terraform failed to download the file because it's not using the credential I have specified. I also confirmed that the server side didn't receive any bearer token. It seems Terraform _assumes_ the download URLs are publicly accessible.

Also notice, the previous calls for service discovery and getting version (e.g. `GET https://ar-terraform-registry.us-central1.run.app/v1/providers/tf-registry-backend/random/3.6.3/download/darwin/arm64`) were all successful because Terraform used the auth token in those requests. I can't make the service accessible to you. But I'd expect any other custom private registry will have the same problem if the download URLs require authentication.

comments.author: liamcervante
comments.body:
Hi @yolocs, thanks for filing this.

I can confirm that Terraform isn't attaching authentication to the follow up requests when retrieving the `downloadUrl` and the `shasumUrl`. This is because both the public and private registries return publicly available URLs for these attributes. This means that it is difficult for us to change this without breaking our primary points of integration.

I do agree that this behaviour isn't documented, I've tagged this issue as a documentation improvement and raised with the internal docs team.

Could you attach temporary credentials to the returned URLs? Or copy the behaviour of the private registry which returns temporary unauthenticated endpoints?

Thanks!

title: Using hashes for sensitive variables in terraform.tfstate
need_summary: Whether Terraform should protect sensitive values in tfstate by hashing them, with the maintainer pointing to issue #516 and the in-progress ephemeral values concept as the relevant source.
security_topic: hashing sensitive variables in state files
question_text: I believe that if for sensitive variable the text in the tfstate file wasn't the plain-text variable but something like a hash digest of the actual value, it would increase security drastically and this would still allow Terraform to check for changes since different input variables lead to different digests.
answer_text:
Hi @wieso-itzi,

We're mainly tracking improvements in this area via #516. The idea of hashing sensitive values is not possible for reasons already outlined in the discussion, but new concepts such as _ephemeral values_ are in the works.

Thanks!
thread_text:
ISSUE #35821: Using hashes for sensitive variables in terraform.tfstate
Author: wieso-itzi
Date: 2024-10-06T12:40:39Z
Labels: enhancement, duplicate
State: closed

[c0]
### Terraform Version

```shell
Terraform v1.9.7
on linux_amd64
```


### Use Cases

Terraform stores the values of variables inside the terraform.tfstate file in plain-text, no matter if they are sensitive or not. The reasoning behing this is that Terraform needs to be aware of changes to these variables in order to properly handle e. g. a terraform apply after changing a variable.

However I believe that if for sensitive variable the text in the tfstate file wasn't the plain-text variable but something like a hash digest of the actual value, it would increase security drastically and this would still allow Terraform to check for changes since different input variables lead to different digests.

### Attempted Solutions

I haven't yet tried or looked into how this could be implemented, but I would be glad to work on the proposed solution.

title: Crash when generating configuration for an imported object that has sensitive attributes
need_summary: Whether the crash while generating config for imported resources with sensitive attributes is a security issue or just a bug, anchored on the maintainer’s explanation in PR #34567 and PR #34525 about sensitive marks and unknown-value handling.
security_topic: crash during config generation for imported resources with sensitive attributes
answer_text:
This actually worked previously because of another bug in Terraform that was fixed in https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/pull/34567. Previously, we weren't properly assigning the sensitive marks from the schema within the plan and instead letting the renderer work out the sensitive status later in the process. With the linked PR we started applying the sensitive marks within the planning graph. Now, when it comes time to generate the config we are not properly handling the sensitive status of certain attributes.

The code that is triggering the crash is checking for unknown values within the imported data. There shouldn't actually be any unknown data returned by the provider and we have started enforcing that with the following PR: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/pull/34525.

I think the fix here is to ensure the same check from #34525 is made within the import execution path, and then remove the check we have for unknown values within the generate config function.

title: `terraform test` Consistently Crashing
need_summary: Whether the `terraform test` crash from referencing locals in file-level test variables was a known bug fixed in Terraform v1.7.1, as identified by pull request #34531 and the prior issue #33780.
security_topic: crash caused by unsupported locals in terraform test file variables
question_text: More info - if I replace all the locals with hardcoded strings (e.g. "my-repo" instead of `local.test_workload_1_repository_name`, it doesn't crash. Are locals not supported, or am I referencing them incorrectly?
answer_text:
Referencing `local` blocks from within variable definitions within Terraform test files will never be supported. Terraform will not load `.tf` files during the initialisation of a test file, instead the test files are initialised first with all their data loaded and then provided into regular Terraform files during the execution of a `run` block.

`terraform test` can already load variables defined directly in `.tfvars` files. It will load auto files automatically, and you can specify particular variable files with the `-var-file` argument. Currently, defining variables via the CLI or variable files is equivalent to defining variables directly within the testing file via the file-level `variables` block. All variables defined in this way must be concrete values, so they can't refer to other variables at all. This is different to variables blocks within run blocks, these can refer to earlier variable definitions.

For example:

```hcl
# main.auto.tfvars

# This is variable file, it only contains static definitions for variables.

global_value = "hello"
```

```hcl
# main.tftest.hcl

# This is our test file.

variables {
  
  # This is a file-level variables block. We can provide more static definitions for variables here.

  bad_value  = var.global_value # Wrong! You can't refer to other variables from this context.
  good_value = "hello"
}

run "test" {
  variables {

    # This is a run-level variables block. We can provide more static definitions here, and we can
    # refer to other variables here as well.

    local_value      = "hello"
    run_good_value   = var.good_value # Right! We can reference the variables defined at the file level.
    run_global_value = var.global_value # Right! We can reference the variables from the files here as well.

  }
}
```

That's a snapshot of the current set of available features. The linked feature request related to this line:

```
  bad_value  = var.global_value # Wrong! You can't refer to other variables from this context.
```

When we implement the linked feature request, we will allow referencing "global" variables (variables defined externally to the test file such as in variable files or on the CLI) within file-level variables blocks. Similar to how you can reference earlier variables from within run-level variables.

Hope this makes sense!

comments.author: liamcervante
comments.body:
Hi @novekm, unfortunately you can't reference configuration locals from within the test file. The test files and their variables are evaluated outside of the Terraform context that the locals and other parts of the configuration are available within. 

Locals and internal variables could rely on parts of the configuration that are only available during / after a plan or apply operation, while the test file has to make all the inputs available at the beginning of each operation, so that kind of workflow is unfortunately not possible.

However, the crash itself is definitely a bug - you should be getting an error message explaining why it's failing at the very least. I see you are running v1.7.0, if you upgrade to v1.7.1 is it still crashing. I think we fixed the crash within https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/pull/34531, which was released in v1.7.1 last week.

Thanks!

comments.author: liamcervante
comments.body:
> locals that are defined in a locals.tf file that's in the same tests directory as main.tftest.hcl.

Terraform test would pick up variables defined within a `terraform.tfvars` [variable file](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/values/variables#variable-definitions-tfvars-files) defined within the testing directory rather than a normal `.tf` file. Unfortunately you can't reference other variables from the global variables block yet. That is the feature request from the issue you've linked here which is currently going through prioritisation.

comments.author: novekm
comments.body:
Ok gotcha, thank you! So to recap - variables are fine as long as they're in a `terraform.tfvars` variable file that resides in the `tests` directory, but `locals.tf` in the same directory will not work (current feature request you mentioned?). Or, do you mean the feature request is to add support to reference say `variables.tf`, `dev.auto.tfvars`, `prod.auto.tfvars`, from the global variables block? 

I'm creating an AWS workshop about how to use this new feature of Terraform within the context of an AWS environment, so I want to make sure I have the correct messaging about what is currently supported 😃

I'll re-run the tests with v1.7.1 and keep you posted on if it crashes again. Thanks!
